heroHeadline: Russia Launches 200+ Drones Across 14 Regions for Second Straight Day — 5 Killed; Trump Says Peace 'Very Close'
heroSubtitle: Russia launched 200+ Shahed-type drones across 14 Ukrainian regions on May 13 — the second consecutive day of mass aerial bombardment since the Trump-brokered 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11) collapsed. In Rivne Oblast a drone struck a residential building, killing 3 and injuring 4; in Kryvyi Rih 2 were killed and 4 wounded. Odesa saw a drone-debris fire near a 9-story building. Power was cut to six front-line regions. Ukraine's military intelligence tracked a daytime wave of 168 Shahed drones at 11:27 local time with additional waves following. On the ground, 170+ combat engagements were reported — Kharkiv and Pokrovsk directions saw the fiercest fighting, with geolocated Russian advances near Sotnytskyi Kozachok. The Kerch Bridge was closed after explosions in Crimea. Ukraine also struck Russian gas facilities in Orenburg (~1,500 km deep). As Russia pounded Ukraine, Trump told reporters departing for Beijing that a peace deal was 'getting very close' — the Kremlin immediately contradicted this, calling it 'a very long road.' Russian personnel losses reached ~1,342,950 by May 13 — sixth consecutive month losses exceed recruitment capacity.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Euronews, CP24, and The Hill. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
